issue.title: Unable to infer schema from json when n rows > 2946

repository.name: polars
repository.description: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames, written in Rust

issue.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

filename= "_hashtags-with-error.json"
df = pl.scan_ndjson(filename).collect()

```



### Log output

```shell
exceptions.ShapeError: unable to vstack, dtypes for column "hashtags" don't match: `list[str]` and `list[null]`
```


### Issue description

originally reported in nodejs polars https://github.com/pola-rs/nodejs-polars/issues/128

note:  if you reduce the `n` rows by 1 it seems to work just fine. 

### Expected behavior

parses json the same as removing the last row in the file. 

### Installed versions

<details>

```
branch = 'main'
```

</details>

body: Note that the problem is a bit more tricky than simply completely null columns, it also applies to a vstack of `List[u64]` and `List[null]` for example.

The same error appears when you `scan_parquet` multiple files via a glob pattern and some files only have null values for a column that others have any other dtype.

```python
import polars as pl

pl.DataFrame({"x": [3.5]}, schema={"x": pl.Float64}).write_parquet("data_a.pq")
pl.DataFrame({"x": [None]}, schema={"x": pl.Null}).write_parquet("data_b.pq")

df = pl.scan_parquet("data_*.pq").collect()
```
Results in
```
polars.exceptions.ShapeError: unable to vstack, dtypes for column "x" don't match: `f64` and `null`
```

@orlp You can achieve your expected behavior using:
```python
import polars as pl

a = pl.DataFrame({"x": [3.5]}, schema={"x": pl.Float64})
b = pl.DataFrame({"x": [None]}, schema={"x": pl.Null})

pl.concat([a,b], how="vertical_relaxed")
```

I wonder if something like this could be implemented for the `pl.scan_*` functions as well.

@Excidion No, we don't want to do implicit casting here. That would allow things such as concatenating `i32` and `i64`. We need to relax the check to allow `null` to be equivalent to any other type, but allow no other coercions.

@Excidion `vertical_relaxed` seems to also be considerably slower (seems less parallel) than `vertical` (haven't rigorously benchmarked but from my pipeline runs... feels this way). I do think this is an obvious issue that should be fixed. 

That said, in the meantime, I have temporarily solved this problem in my code by detecting all_null columns and casting/dropping them before I do a `pl.concat([a,b], how='vertical')`

This issue was initially met in `read_ndjson` here: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/11496#issuecomment-1766963339
```python
import io
import polars as pl

text1 = '{"key": [1, 2]}'
text2 = '{"key1": [1, 2]}'


file = io.StringIO(
    '\n'.join([text1 for _ in range(100)]) + 
    '\n' + 
    '\n'.join([text2 for _ in range(100)])
    )
pl.read_ndjson(file, schema={"key": pl.List(pl.UInt32)})
RuntimeError: BindingsError: "lengths don't match: unable to vstack, dtypes for column \"key\" don't match: `list[u32]` and `list[null]`"
```
So basically I can not implement suggested workarounds like `casting/dropping all_null columns` or `using pl.concat([a,b], how="vertical_relaxed")`, because I have ndjson file with dynamic schema.

Maybe someone can suggest temporary solution until this fixed?

@s-b90 Can you read the input as a single string and use the `.str` methods?

```python
# ndjson = file.read()
(pl.select(json = pl.lit(ndjson).str.split("\n"))
   .explode("json")
   .select(pl.col("json").str.json_extract(infer_schema_length=None))
   .unnest("json")
)

# DeprecationWarning: `json_extract` is deprecated. It has been renamed to `json_decode`.
# shape: (200, 2)
# ┌───────────┬───────────┐
# │ key       ┆ key1      │
# │ ---       ┆ ---       │
# │ list[i64] ┆ list[i64] │
# ╞═══════════╪═══════════╡
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null      │
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null      │
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null      │
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null      │
# │ …         ┆ …         │
# │ null      ┆ [1, 2]    │
# │ null      ┆ [1, 2]    │
# │ null      ┆ [1, 2]    │
# │ null      ┆ [1, 2]    │
# └───────────┴───────────┘
```

@s-b90 Nice one.

Using your example, I did notice some other odd behaviour.

(I removed `schema=` for testing)

For me, it works up until `range(64)`

```python
text1 = '{"key": [1, 2]}'
text2 = '{"key1": [1, 2]}'


file = io.StringIO(
    '\n'.join([text1 for _ in range(64)]) + 
    '\n' + 
    '\n'.join([text2 for _ in range(64)])
)
pl.read_ndjson(file)

# shape: (128, 2)
# ┌───────────┬───────────┐
# │ key       ┆ key1      │
# │ ---       ┆ ---       │
# │ list[i64] ┆ list[i64] │
# ╞═══════════╪═══════════╡
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null      │
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null      │
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null      │
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null      │
# │ …         ┆ …         │
# │ null      ┆ [1, 2]    │
# │ null      ┆ [1, 2]    │
# │ null      ┆ [1, 2]    │
# │ null      ┆ [1, 2]    │
# └───────────┴───────────┘
```
`range(65)` returns the vstack error, but if I add an extra `\n` it works again.

```python
file = io.StringIO(
    '\n'.join([text1 for _ in range(65)]) + 
    '\n' + 
    '\n'.join([text2 for _ in range(65)])
    + '\n' # new
)
```

This works all the way up to `range(99)`.

At `range(100)` there is no error, but it produces only the `key` column.

I'm not sure if these are all the same underlying problem or not.
I can confirm that. @orlp should we open separate issue for that, or this is related issues?

issue.title: fix: support `append`/`extend` with null series (#11824)

repository.name: polars
repository.description: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames, written in Rust

issue.body:
This PR is a partial fix for issue https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/11824. It solves the case when one cannot `df1.vstack(df2)` because eg. `df1["x"].dtype == pl.Int64` but `df2["x"].dtype == pl.Null`.

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/11824 also mentions a more complex example, when we get conflict between eg. `List[Int64]` and `List[Null]`. This is related to behaviour introduced by PR https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/12677 which produces these `List[Null]` columns when parsing empty JSON arrays.
